question: Evaluate $$\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\left(-\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)\right)+\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\left(-\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)\right).$$
explanation:
Principal value of the inverse tangent term
The principal range of $\tan^{-1}x$ is $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$. Using the period $\pi$ of tangent, $$\tan\left(-\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)=\tan\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right).$$ Hence, $$\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\left(-\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)\right)=-\frac{\pi}{4}.$$

Principal value of the inverse cosine term
Cosine is even, so $$\cos\left(-\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)=\cos\frac{7\pi}{6}=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.$$ The angle in $[0,\pi]$ having cosine $-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ is $\frac{5\pi}{6}$.

Addition of principal values
Therefore, the required value is $$-\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{5\pi}{6}=\frac{-3\pi+10\pi}{12}=\frac{7\pi}{12}.$$
